sections.html:
Smith County sends Tyler's tax bills and collects for every taxing unit in the county. The office sits at 1517 W. Front St., Tyler, TX 75702, with a mailing box at P.O. Box 2011 and a phone line at (903) 590-2920. Hours are 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., open through lunch.

One Tyler bill can carry several lines: the city, Smith County, Tyler Junior College and a school district. The school district depends on the address, since some Tyler properties sit in Whitehouse ISD or Chapel Hill ISD instead of Tyler ISD. Your statement shows which one applies to you.

sections.h2: Tyler property tax rates, tax year 2026
sections.html:
These are the 2026 figures, each stated per $100 of value: $0.242063 for the city, $0.374088 for Smith County, $0.210312 for Tyler Junior College and $0.835000 for Tyler ISD.

Addresses served by Whitehouse ISD (0.964900) or Chapel Hill ISD (1.072900) use those school rates instead. Call the tax office to confirm the rate on your exact parcel.

The city rate is down more than 50 percent from the mid 1990s, when it stood at $0.5336 in 1994-95. It reached a low of $0.1990 in 2007-08, climbed to $0.2699 in 2021-22 and then slid each year to $0.236452 in 2025-26.

This year's 2026-27 rate of $0.242063 is higher than last year's and above the city's no-new-revenue rate of 0.232965. The city also commits two cents of its rate to the street fund, equal to $2.4 million.

  • 1994-95: $0.5336
  • 2007-08: $0.1990
  • 2021-22: $0.2699
  • 2025-26: $0.236452
  • 2026-27: $0.242063

Between 2022 and 2026 most Tyler-area rates dropped, and the county's went up.

  • Smith County: 0.330000 in 2022, 0.347264 in 2023, 0.364231 in 2024 and 2025, then 0.374088 in 2026.
  • Tyler ISD: 1.179300 in 2022, 0.960000 in 2023, 0.910000 in 2024, 0.845000 in 2025 and 0.835000 in 2026.
  • Tyler Junior College: 0.188001 in 2022, then 0.185068 in 2025 and 0.210312 in 2026.
  • City of Tyler: 0.261850 in 2022 and 0.242063 in 2026.

The statement you receive shows your exact numbers.

Tyler's sales tax rate is 8.25 percent. That splits into 6.25 percent for the State of Texas, 1 percent for the city's general fund, 0.5 percent for Tyler's One Half Cent Sales Tax Corporation and 0.5 percent for Smith County.

Nightly rentals owe hotel occupancy tax and short-term rental tax, paid through the city's portal at tylertx.hdlgov.com. A house that was ever rented that way is worth a call to the city finance department before listing, to rule out unpaid occupancy tax.

Tyler holds about 113,723 residents, 7.4 percent more than in 2020. Owners occupy 55.4 percent of homes, and the median value of those homes is $235,300. Rent runs a median $1,252 monthly. Owning costs $1,743 a month with a mortgage and $664 without. Moderate prices mean the school exemption takes a meaningful bite out of a typical bill.

Statements land in mailboxes near October 1. Paying any time before the end of January costs nothing extra, but a bill still open on February 1 is delinquent.

The first day of delinquency adds 6 percent in penalty and 1 percent in interest. Another point of penalty arrives monthly, reaching 12 percent on July 1, and interest runs one percent per month. If a unit hires a collection attorney, up to 20 percent more can land on the account. A split is possible for some owners: half by November 30, the balance by June 30 the next year. The Smith County office can say whether you qualify.

On the school side, a homestead loses $140,000 of value. Owners 65 or older, or disabled, lose another $60,000. Most exemption forms go to the appraisal district ahead of May 1.

State law adds these protections for Tyler homes:

  • Appraised value on a residence homestead may climb at most 10 percent a year, counting from the year after it first qualifies.
  • A school-tax ceiling for seniors and disabled owners, which can follow them to a new Texas homestead.
  • A disabled veteran's exemption of $5,000, $7,500, $10,000 or $12,000 depending on rating, with the whole homestead exempt at 100 percent.

The city, county and college can each add a local exemption of their own. The Smith County Appraisal District has the current percentages.

If the appraisal looks high, the review board wants your protest by May 15, or 30 days after you receive the notice if that comes later. Notices for single-family homesteads are mailed about April 1, and hearings open in mid May.

Unhappy with the ruling? Options include district court, binding arbitration, or a SOAH hearing if the board value tops $1,000,000. Keep paying: an appeal never pauses the bill, and you owe at least the undisputed tax by the delinquency date.

sections.h2: Who pays what when Tyler closes
sections.html:
Each January 1, a lien for that year's tax attaches to the property, and the January 1 owner is on the hook. The contract decides how the year's bill is divided at closing.

If you sell mid-year, obtain a written balance from the Smith County Tax Office ahead of closing. The title company deducts it from your proceeds. Cash deals run the same way, since back tax must be cleared before title passes.

Nothing carries your exemption over to the buyer. If you had none, a buyer who closes after January 1 may still apply for the remainder of that year. Heirs without a recorded deed bring an ownership affidavit and a death certificate.

Title work moves faster when you have things ready. First, your latest Smith County statement, which breaks out each unit's charge and names your school district. Add proof of your homestead exemption, any protest paperwork, and the deed or ownership affidavit if the house came through an estate.

Next, ask the tax office for a payoff on this year's bill. For a former nightly rental, clear any occupancy tax with the city. A cash buyer skips lender approval, though it will still want clear title, so the same payoffs apply. With these in hand you can compare a listing, a private sale and a cash offer on equal terms.

faqs.q: What does the city of Tyler charge?
faqs.a: $0.242063 per $100 for 2026-2027, though county, junior college and school district rates are added to your full bill.
At the Smith County Tax Office, 1517 W. Front St., Tyler, phone (903) 590-2920. That one office takes payment for the city and every other jurisdiction in the county.

faqs.q: What day does a bill go delinquent?
faqs.a: The morning of February 1, when the unpaid balance gains a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest.

faqs.q: Is every Tyler address in Tyler ISD?
faqs.a: No. A few properties within Tyler belong to Whitehouse ISD or Chapel Hill ISD. Your statement names your district.

faqs.q: What exemption comes with a Tyler homestead?
faqs.a: Schools exempt $140,000 of a home's value, plus $60,000 more for seniors and disabled owners. For city and county amounts, ask the Smith County Appraisal District.
